project.name: Apollo
project.description: Apollo is a reliable, centralized configuration management system designed for microservice environments. It enables applications across different clusters and environments to manage configurations from a unified interface with real-time hot-release capabilities, versioned rollback support, and grayscale deployment options. The system comprises multiple service tiers: a Config Service (read-only client-facing configuration delivery), an Admin Service (write-side configuration management), a Portal (web UI for operators), and SDKs for Java and .NET clients that support both framework-agnostic and Spring/Spring Boot integration.
project.architecture_summary: Apollo is organized as a layered, multi-service architecture with clear separation of concerns. The codebase is divided into distinct service modules (admin-service, config-service, portal) and shared infrastructure (apollo-biz, apollo-common). The architecture follows standard Spring Boot patterns with REST controllers, service layer abstractions, JPA entity models, and Spring Data repositories. Cross-cutting concerns are handled through AOP aspects (for namespace locking, audit logging), servlet filters (for authentication and authorization), and event-driven patterns (for configuration change notifications). The system employs multiple caching strategies (in-memory Guava caches, Redis-backed sessions), distributed locking for concurrent modification safety, and supports pluggable service discovery backends (Eureka, database, Kubernetes, Consul, Nacos, Zookeeper). Authentication is flexible and supports multiple mechanisms: basic Spring Security, LDAP, OIDC/JWT, and legacy Ctrip-specific implementations.
